headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from Khoj’s shared indexed notes feeding Rasa’s external chat channels; capability conflict is limited by Rasa’s allowlisted egress and no write access is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can expose retrieved content into chat, while Rasa ingests text from external channels like Slack, Telegram, and Twilio. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Khoj content is forwarded into Rasa without sanitization. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieval output is forwarded into Rasa conversation text without filtering, prompt injection is possible.
IF Rasa treats incoming channel text as instructions rather than untrusted user content, attacker-controlled notes can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that treats all retrieved text as untrusted.
Strip or escape instruction-like markup before passing Khoj output to Rasa.
Require a human review step for any retrieved note that will be relayed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Khoj to Rasa inputs.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents with a non-textual handoff format.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and its network egress is broad. Rasa handles text and voice and can send messages through external channels such as Slack or Twilio. If Khoj content is surfaced into Rasa, sensitive notes can leak into third-party messaging infrastructure. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium fits the documented-but-inferred pathway.
conditions: IF Khoj indexed notes contain sensitive personal data and are forwarded to Rasa, leakage can occur.
IF Rasa relays conversation text to Slack, Telegram, or Twilio, that text leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Limit Khoj retrieval to non-sensitive collections.
Disable or restrict Rasa outbound channel connectors for sensitive conversations.
Redact secrets and personal identifiers before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention on the integration.
requires-engineering: separate storage and transport domains for the two agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Rasa’s profile only documents allowlisted network egress and no write or git capability. With no overlapping mutable resource writes documented, direct capability conflict is limited; uncertainty does not justify escalation because the profiles already constrain the overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF Rasa is extended with filesystem or git write tools, coordination risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared paths.
Avoid mounting the same writable workspace into both runtimes.
Use separate service accounts and directories.
requires-engineering: add file-locking if shared writes are introduced.
requires-engineering: gate any future write capability behind explicit orchestration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and documents, and Rasa is a dialogue system that can act on incoming text from messaging channels. If Rasa treats Khoj output as authoritative, retrieval errors can cascade into incorrect replies or actions. The profiles do not show verification or downstream action safeguards, so the interaction exists in a default-ish integration but is not proven dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF Khoj output is copied into Rasa responses without verification, errors propagate.
IF Rasa uses retrieved text as the basis for customer-facing replies, misinformation can be sent outward.
mitigations: Require citation checks before Rasa sends a reply.
Add a confidence threshold for Khoj-derived facts.
Route uncertain answers to a human agent.
requires-engineering: implement structured fact extraction before response generation.
requires-engineering: add regression tests for retrieval hallucinations.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Rasa handles text and voice and can integrate with third-party messaging channels. The profiles do not show a residency, retention, or certification mismatch, so only a compliance-overlap gap is evident. Because the other agent is not cited for a specific violation, the risk remains low and limited to policy alignment work.
conditions: IF personal notes are routed from Khoj into a regulated Rasa deployment, policy review is required.
IF retention settings differ between the two systems for the same conversation data, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Document the data classes shared between systems.
Align retention and deletion settings across both agents.
Restrict regulated data from entering Rasa channels.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement in the integration.
requires-engineering: obtain a formal DPA or equivalent review for the deployment.
